about.title: About
about.content:
BSc Aerospace Engineering, Polytechnic University of Milan. MSc Artificial Intelligence, VU & UvA Amsterdam (first gen graduate!)
Software engineer with a BSc in Aerospace Engineering and four years of experience working on complex systems, from safety critical flight simulation software to large scale, event-driven platforms processing millions of events per day. I have a background in real-time systems, distributed architectures, and hardware/software integration.
After working 4 years full-time as a system software engineer, I am currently completing a dual MSc in Artificial Intelligence at Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam and the University of Amsterdam to deepen my expertise in machine learning and data-driven systems. I’m driven by technically challenging problems and enjoy working at the intersection of software, data, and complex systems.

projects.title: Projects
projects.content:
SiagaFlood: flood early warning for rural Indonesia
Group project for ICT for the Global South (VU Amsterdam, 2026). SiagaFlood is a flood early-warning system for rural Indonesia. I designed its radio voice backup, which reaches residents that SMS alerts don’t: a local coordinator reviews the draft alert, approves the SMS, then plays a ready-made message in Bahasa Indonesia on community radio and marks it as broadcast. We built a working prototype with both an Indonesian and an English interface.
Robot arm trained from human preferences
Group project for Human-Interactive Agent Learning (VU Amsterdam). A robot arm learns to pick up a banana and place it on a plate. We learned the reward from human preferences with APReL, added expert demonstrations to the replay buffer, and trained the control policy with AWAC.
Code on GitHub
Sim-to-Real Reinforcement Learning for Mobile Robotics: From Simulation to Real-World Deployment on Robobo
Designed and implemented an end-to-end reinforcement learning pipeline to train policies in CoppeliaSim and transfer them directly to a physical Robobo robot. Built Gym-compatible environments, engineered low-dimensional vision features, and applied Soft Actor-Critic for continuous control. Successfully solved obstacle avoidance, object foraging, and object pushing with consistent sim-to-real transfer. Focus on robustness, sensor calibration, and reducing the reality gap.
Code on GitHub
Natural language processing: Zipf’s law, n-grams and word vectors
Group assignment for Natural Language Processing (VU Amsterdam, 2026). We tested Zipf’s law on the Brown corpus, built n-gram language models, and worked with word vectors.
Code on GitHub
Shock absorbers
The shock absorber is the one item that is common to all current landing gears. Some don’t have tires, brakes, antiskid devices, retraction systems, or steering systems, but all of them have some form of shock absorber. While the carrier landing has sometimes been called a “controlled crash”, it would be a complete catastrophe without the shock absorber.
Retrospective analysis of El Al 1982
This short retrospective analysis shows the events and factors that, on 4 October 1992, led to the crash of El Al flight 1982, operated by a Boeing 747-200F. To do this we used two methods: ISAAC and ADREP.
Orbit characterisation
The purpose of this report is to establish an efficient transfer strategy that can allow us to successfully move an object (e.g. a satellite) revolving around the Earth between two given orbits.
